page: Microsoft Azure E64-16s_v5 is a memory-optimized virtual machine from the ESv5 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by an Intel Xeon 8370C processor operating at 2.8 GHz. The configuration includes 16 dedicated vCPUs derived from 8 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. A key hardware characteristic is its massive memory allocation of 512.0 GB of RAM, translating to 32.0 GB per core. It does not include local storage or GPUs, but it is Premium Storage capable.

Benchmark results place this instance in the average performance category for its hardware class. The single-core stress-ng performance is recorded at 1898.58, while multi-core performance reaches 15528.57. Memory bandwidth tests show a read-only small block cached speed of 838.79 GB/sec, dropping to 96.24 GB/sec for large uncached blocks, and a write speed of 55.35 GB/sec. The system achieves a PassMark CPU score of 21418.74 and a memory score of 2721.31. For database workloads, it handles 15.75 million Redis SET operations per second and scores 8079.39 on PassMark database operations.

The primary tradeoff of the E64-16s_v5 is the lack of local NVMe storage and GPU accelerators, meaning all storage must be attached externally via Premium Storage. However, the high memory-to-vCPU ratio provides excellent qualitative cost efficiency for memory-bound workloads that do not require proportional compute scaling. This makes the instance highly suitable for large in-memory databases, caching layers, enterprise applications, and data-intensive processing tasks that benefit from a 512.0 GB memory footprint without paying for 64 full vCPUs.
